Looking for a miracle. IVERMECTIN

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Its SAHPRA versus some doctors as the debate about Ivermectin heats up. Promising says Stellenbosch university but not conclusive

Unique Selling Point:
A very hot topic as South Africans wait for life saving vaccines and there is still no magic bullet against Covid-19
( Due to time constraints I am putting in the original proposal with the knowledge that this has been fried and has new information in it

Summary:
In January, across the platteland a low level frenzy took place. Farmers, doctors, and regular people inundated Ko-ops to get their stash of the veterinary medicine IVOMEC-
an anti- parasitic for their sheep and cattle that is the most profitable veterinary medicine of all time. Why?

Because they have been convinced that this medicine will keep them Covid or at least death free, and even if our scientists who are some of the best in the world have expressed their reservations, men in two tone shirts are injecting themselves, their families and their workers with Ivermectin. When in early January SAHPRA banned the import of Ivermectin, it didn’t take long for the criminals and opportunists to jump on the band wagon and bring in about 150 thousand contraband tablets in their luggage. For their efforts they were arrested and are out on R50 000 bail.

So does it work and is it safe? That is the million dollar question and one that Carte Blanche will try and answer by speaking to a doctor on the frontline a world renowned scientist and

As 2021 dawned we all hoped that the worst of the pandemic was over. But that spiky little virus is not done with us yet. 30 000 deaths, a rapidly increasing second wave and a tricksy variant has our health department on the back foot once again. We are out of options and out of money, and our vaccine rollout could still take months before it really makes an impact on most of us. So, South Africans are doing what they always do – they are making a plan, and refusing to wait for the high priests of medicine to give them the go ahead -they are taking Ivermectin in a desperate and reckless attempt to keep the virus at bay.



Further information:
THE FRONT LINE COVID CRITICAL CARE ALLIANCE AND DR KORY

The frenzy began when an American physician, Dr Kory appeared at a Senate hearing in December. He told the committee that he belonged to a group of highly published physicians in the world and they had been reviewing the literature of all drugs to try and find a solution to Covid 19.

“We have done nothing but try to figure out how to identify a repurpose available drugs to treat this illness.”

He expressed his concern that the solutions being touted were about novel and expensive pharmaceutical drugs. He said he was “severely troubled by the fact that the FDA, the NAH and the CDC have done nothing to review repurposed drugs to treat this disease.”

He said: “We have 100 years of medicine development and we do not know of a task force that has been constituted to evaluate available drugs.”

He says Ivermectin has a miraculous impact but he doesn’t want to be sensational when he says that. “It’s a scientific evaluation based on mountains of data that has emerged in the last few months. It basically obliterates transmission of this virus. If you take it he says you will not get sick.”

He quotes a trial from Argentina where he says 800 health care workers used it as a prophylactic and not one not get sick. He says it has immense and potent anti- viral activity.
He quotes different trials and says four randomized trials in hospitals show reduced mortality.
“It is proving to be a wonder drug” says Dr Kory.” Its already won the Nobel prize for medicine in 2015 for the eradication of parasitic diseases.

With this kind of sales pitch it’s hard to blame the farmers for trusting an American physician in a white coat, telling a senate hearing that the drug works. Who can blame them for putting their trust in a first world doctor, when our own president told them less than two weeks ago that the vaccine was still months away, and the health ministers webinar gave few specifics and was criticized by Dr Mahdi as aspirational rather than a specific plan?

But we have been down this road before – most notably with Hydroxychloroquine- touted as a miracle by no less than the President of the USA. And we know where that went. Not only was the drug dangerous it also didn’t work.

As conspiracy theorists jumped back on their bandwagon, the Department of health did ask our scientists and top pharmacists for a quick review . On the 21st December they summarized their finding
•
• The overall quality of the randomized trials involving ivermectin in COVID‐19 patients is extremely low.
• From the available randomised control trial evidence, ivermectin is not superior to placebo in terms of viral load reduction or clinical progression. There is no evidence from randomised control trials for any reduction in mortality.
Eligible patients with COVID‐19 in South Africa should be considered for enrolment in relevant therapeutic trials.
In a nutshell they recommended that Ivermectin not be used for adults with Covid-19. Soon after the South African Health products regulatory authority banned the importation of ivermectin.

SAHPRA chief executive Dr Boitumelo Semete-Makokotlela said: “Our stance is unambiguous. This drug is not approved by Sahpra and any attempt to import it into the country will be dealt with by Sahpra’s regulatory compliance unit in conjunction with law enforcement agencies such as the SAPS and the SIU.”
Semete-Makokotlela said: “If any member of the public is aware of such transgressions, please contact Deon Poovan, senior manager of Sahpra’s Inspectorate and Regulatory Compliance on deon.poovan@sahpra.org.za”
“At present, there is no confirmatory clinical evidence available for the use of ivermectin in the management of Covd-19 infections,” said Semete-Makokotlela.
“In terms of safety and efficacy, there is no evidence to support the use of ivermectin and we do not have any clinical trial evidence to justify its use.

By Monday this week the battle over this drug began to intensify. Enter the Ivermectin interest group. Eleven scientists from KZN that are petitioning the health department to change their stance on ivermectin. This is what they had to say in an open letter:
The Ivermectin Interest Group ("IIG") is a grouping of clinicians, public health specialists, community health workers and scientists that have an interest in exploring the potential of the medicine Ivermectin to both prevent and treat COVID-19. While we fully endorse the pursuit and implementation of all available evidence-based vaccines, as they are essential to ending the pandemic, we wish to ensure that the potential of promising preventive and therapeutic measures, including drugs, be fully and urgently investigated.
IVERMECTIN
Currently, the use of Ivermectin is controversial for sound scientific reasons. We acknowledge that the drug has not been indicated for use in COVID-19 prophylaxis or treatment, either locally or by the major regulatory bodies globally. However, we must note that Ivermectin has been the subject of a number of studies and reviews, including a review funded by the World Health Organisation (WHO) as part of the ACT Accelerator and UNITAID programmes (Hill et al., 2020) that concluded that urgent further trials are required and that results anticipated from clinical trials currently underway will be available in January 2021 and could provide the numbers required for a meta-analysis to provide a reliable outcome.
Dr Andrew Hill Sr, a respected academic and World Health Organisation (WHO) researcher who has been tasked, as part of the Unitaid ACT Accelerator initiative to improve access to COVID-19 treatments and diagnostics, recently reported at an international ivermectin conference a meta-analysis of data from the first 11 randomised controlled trials that have been identified. This meta-analysis, while still ongoing, points towards the significant promise of Ivermectin as a low cost, widely available therapy potentially useful in COVID-19. His finding thus far, in the trials totalling 1452 patients, is that ivermectin treatment is associated with faster time to viral clearance, shorter duration of hospitalisation, 43% higher rates in clinical recovery (95% CI 21-67%), and a profound 83% improvement in survival (95% C.I. 65-92%). Other reviews that draw similar conclusions (Appendix 1) and national health authorities are also looking at Ivermectin (Appendix 2). The ivermectin studies stand out because there are virtually no studies showing a negative outcome.
There is a plethora of clinical research trial results supporting the efficacy of Ivermectin for COVID-19 prophylaxis and treatment, including both small and large randomised controlled trials and observational studies reported in peer- reviewed journals and pre-publication websites. A living systematic review of all papers is required in South Africa, to monitor this literature and further support meta-analysis data to gain a clearer picture of the effect of Ivermectin on COVID- 19.
A POLITICAL PARTY WEIGHS IN
Then on the 3rd of January an attorney’s letter was sent to the minister of health, and the CEO and board of SAHPRA from the National Freedom party. They want a meeting with our health leaders to discuss the use and possible testing of ivermectin. In the letter they have given the DOH until today Wednesday 6th January to respond, failing which they are going to approach the high court for relief. At the end of January SAHPRA agreed to compassionate use under a section 21 application.
DISCUSSION POINTS FOR DR SEMETE AND PROFESSOR HELEN REES


• Criticism against SAHPRA for its earlier stance
• SAHPRA looking to FDA and EMA for guidance on IVERMECTIN
• Reasons for the section 21 compassionate use
• Widespread use of Ivermectin by doctors
• Criticism against SAHPRA from both sides – buckling under pressure from lobby groups or not going far enough for some doctors
• Response to doctors saying SAHPRA decision is administrative nightmare
• Concerns that doctors will not adhere to the admin and dismiss SAHPRA guidelines
• Public no longer listen to scientists and google Dr Kory and take veterinary medicine
• Dangers of taking veterinary medicine – 1m dosages versus 3ml dosages
• Danger of unregulated Ivermectin coming into the country
• Clinical trials – no money in these for pharmaceutical companies – so no RCT done here
• Merck donation for River blindness – 4 billion doses administered why did SAHPRA say it was not a safe medicine.
• Free State university not being open and transparent about trials – not sure why
• Allegations against SAHPRA by some doctors that they are preventing people from getting life saving medication
• IVERMECTIN Silver bullet or another Hydroxychloroquine saga
• COMMENTS ON THE FLCCC studies – Dr Kory

• Comments on DR ANDREW HILL’s recent submission to doctors on the 21st January
• Various studies showing viral clearance after 5 days
• Consistent conclusions across the countries that Ivermectin reduces viral clearance
• Trends where fewer people are dying than in the control
• 18 randomized studies and more coming – response to these studies
• Cochrane risk of bias assessments
• Next steps using the Cochrane criteria to evaluate the new RCT coming out in Feb.
• Meta -analysis by Dr Tess Lawrie – response
• FLCCC studies and the P values of the MATH + protocol
• Dosages and toxicity
• More evidence needed before decisions are taken
• Next Steps – are scientists constantly evaluating the new data or is the decision now taken by SAHPRA final

FINAL SCRIPT IVERMECTIN FACT AND SCRIPT CHECKED TX SUNDAY 14th FEB 2021

Commentary One
When Japanese bio-chemist Satoshi Omura dug out a soil sample on a golf course, he had just stumbled upon a new class of drug called Avermectins. The drug was later developed as Ivermectin, and would become the most profitable veterinary medicine in the world - used by farmers everywhere

Phil Rawlins
It’s a very good product, it protects the animals against parasites

Commentary Two
Ivermectin also earned Omura and its co- founder the Nobel prize in 2015. Because apart from its success with animals, Ivermectin also worked on people. Over four billion treatments have been donated by pharmaceutical company Merck in an ongoing effort to eliminate river blindness and elephantiasis, in remote tropical regions

Link
Ivermectin is not registered for human consumption in SA, so it’s quite difficult to come by, on the other hand, the veterinary formulation is usually quite easily available. You just needed to go down to your local co-op

Commentary Three
But that all changed in early January, because WhatsApp groups across the platteland were abuzz that Ivermectin could also possibly work against Covid-19. Phil Rawlins is a dairy and sheep farmer, and uses Ivermectin on his herds, but suddenly it was difficult to find.

Farmer Phil
We struggle to get Ivermectin. The shelves are empty, it looks like people are going crazy ko-ops are not just for the farmers anymore. City people are also coming to buy Ivermectin

Commentary Four
Professor Vinny Naidoo, a veterinary pharmacologist and dean of the faculty of veterinary science, is astonished by this scramble for the veterinary formulation of Ivermectin

Professor
So we have received reports of Ivermectin being bought in mass volumes from all the farm shops, in fact it’s almost impossible to find Ivermectin anywhere. We have reports of farmers prescribing to family and friends, people selling it at excessively high prices. The drug is actually very cheap- R1.50 per ml, and I heard reports of people selling it for R100 per dose, so its created this black market and that in itself is dangerous.

LINK
By April last year as deaths began mounting, scientists and doctors started experimenting with drugs that are already available. In Australia they added a single dose of Ivermectin into a petri dish with the virus and cell culture. Within 48 hours the virus was dead
Commentary Five
But drugs that are miracles in a petri dish, can still disappoint in a human body.
Hydroxychloroquine was hyped as a Covid treatment, but later found to be a dud. Professor Helen Rees, chairperson of the South African health products regulatory authority, explains

Helen Rees
Some things might look very hopeful we saw that with Remdesivir with a smaller study, followed by a larger study that said it didn’t work. We saw that with Hydroxychloroquine, hopeful data initially from smaller studies, larger studies didn’t work.

Commentary Six
As Covid-19 overwhelmed hospitals in Argentina, Mexico and Egypt, doctors had little to work with, and turned to Ivermectin in desperation.
By December of 2020, a group of international physicians, who examined those early trials, told a United States senate hearing, Ivermectin could be the answer to the disease

Dr Kory
mountains of data have emerged in the last few months. It basically obliterates transmission of this virus. If you take it you will not get sick.”

Commentary Seven
It was largely this presentation by Dr Kory of the Frontline Covid-19 Critical care alliance that sent South African farmers to storm the ko-ops.

Phil Rawlins
If I am honest I don’t think it’s dangerous. I have used it myself and I still feel good.

Professor
There are numerous concerns when it comes to using a veterinary formulation. Firstly it’s illegal to use a veterinary formulation , secondly we don’t know anything about this formulation.

Phil Rawlins
We took a chance at this stage. I must say I feel good, I am going to carry on taking it and hope I don’t get Covid

Masa
Prof talk to us a little bit more about the side effects?
Professor
We know that Ivermectin in animals can cause paralysis just like in the parasite in interferes with the nerve function, it interferes with the brain, and you can have a progressive type of stupor, the animal appears blind and they go into a coma and it’s very difficult to recover them from that. It’s no different to the side-effects you see in people.




Commentary eight
Alarmed by what was unfolding, the South African Health products regulatory authority, declared Ivermectin illegal and banned its import. That set it on a collision course with a group of SA doctors. Dr Boitumelo Semete-Makokotlela is the CEO

Masa
Why did SAHPRA ban the importation of Ivermectin?
Dr Semete
So any drug that is not registered by us as a regulator, is regarded as a drug used unlawfully because you are not complying with the medicines act. We’ve got reports of businessmen just bringing in this product and they are not authorized some of them have no experience in the pharmaceutical sector so it does pose a risk for the public.

Commentary nine
But the banning led to two unintended consequences. The first was that smugglers jumped on the band wagon. Late in January six Indian nationals were arrested and later charged for illegally importing around R6 million rand’s worth of Ivermectin in their luggage

Magistrate Schutte
The matter is now postponed to 16th March 2021. Bail is fixed in the amount of R50 000

Masa
What we saw happen after that were hundreds of thousands of tablets smuggled into the country. That created an even bigger problem?

Dr Boitumelo- Semete
No it did. It did. Our law enforcement teams were inundated with inspections of these products. That is one of the reasons we said let’s have a controlled mechanism where we would know who was licensed and anyone else not licensed they will have to deal with the might of the law

Up sound Facebook farmer
Maybe it tastes very bad. I will squirt it at the back of my mouth

Commentary ten
The second consequence was that patients began to self -medicate with the veterinary medicine as a prophylaxis.

Facebook Farmer
On the contrary it doesn’t taste bad at all

Commentary eleven
And as the second wave intensified, patients began to pressurize their doctors.
At the time Johannesburg doctor Paul Freinkel, shared his thoughts in a letter to online newspaper Daily Maverick



Paul Freinkel up sound
The threat of death hangs in the very air we breathe, it has not felt so close, or so frequent since my internship at the peak of the HIV pandemic ...the punishing hours, the exhaustion, the helplessness the fear of infection...

Now we wear masks visors and gowns modern amulets warding off unseen demons Government then didn’t care. Now we uncle Cyril’s ...while we watch our patients suffocate in their own body fluids

Masa
The million dollar question is, does it work for covid-19?
Dr Freinkel
One has to look at the data and the data is starting to say that it probably will. And it looks like it is, but we need more data.

Commentary Twelve
Dr Freinkel read extensively, independently evaluating the 2020 trials cited by the Front line covid critical care alliance, as well as the data from scientist Dr Andrew Hill, and he came to his own conclusions.

Masa
So would you say it's safe?
Dr Freinkel
It's not without its complications, every drug has its benefits and side effects. The benefit must always outweigh the risk. And it would appear, given the safety profile of ivermectin, that the potential benefits as far as the data shows us now and it is incomplete, but the potential benefit far outweighs the potential risk if used correctly.

Commentary Thirteen
What is also dividing doctors and scientists is the dosage for Covid, and only randomized clinical trials can put that to rest.

Link
Randomized clinical trials are the gold standard to measure a drug’s efficacy. In the case of ivermectin – there have been clinical trials that show positive results. But our scientists aren’t accepting them.

Commentary Fourteen
Professor Rees says bigger trials are needed

Professor Helen Rees
So Ivermectin looked promising- the problem is that the studies that were designed to evaluate Ivermectin were small studies, not targeting the same groups of patients, had different indications different dosages, different, formulations and because of that, it’s been extremely difficult to make very firm conclusions

Masa
Is that the reason why you and other South African scientists aren’t accepting the results coming from all over the world?
Professor Helen Rees
No it’s not a matter of not accepting the results, what is happening for SAHPRA three different national official bodies have looked at the data. We need large studies that are properly designed to answer this question one way or another. So at the moment we have this situation where we can’t say it works and we can’t say it doesn’t work – and we also need to know if it does work is it safe in the kind of doses that would be required to make it work. We don’t have any of those answers and against that backdrop we need more science.

Commentary Fifteen
And more science is coming. Stellenbosch university is part of the together Covid-19 trial consortium and they are currently in discussions to test ivermectin and other drugs, during our anticipated third wave. In the meantime SAHPRA have softened its stance and doctors can now use Ivermectin on a case by case basis.

Paul
When this argument first started, we had different army camps, almost religious in their points of view. We will. We won't. We want to use it. You won't. And now I think I think people are coming to the senses and saying, well, what's the harm? And leaving it to a doctor to decide, which is what doctors are trained to do on the balance of probability is it going to help and is it safe?

THE END 11 02.



PROMO ONE
There are only two real questions in the Ivermectin debate. Does it work for covid-19 and is it safe. And it’s the answers to those questions that have divided the scientific community

PROMO TWO
The Ivermectin debate rages on, as our scientists call for better clinical trials to find out once and for all if this anti parasitic drug is the miracle some doctors say it is.

PROMO THREE
Doctors are repurposing drugs, hoping they will work against the Corona virus. There has been hype and disappointment. Now Ivermectin is the latest drug dividing scientists.

CHECKED TX SUNDAY 14th FEB 2021 Commentary One When Japanese bio-chemist Satoshi Omura dug out a soil sample on a golf course, he had just stumbled upon a new class of drug called Avermectins. The drug was later developed as Ivermectin, and would become the most profitable veterinary medicine in the world - used by farmers everywhere Phil Rawlins It’s a very good product, it protects the animals against parasites Commentary Two Ivermectin also earned Omura and its co- founder the Nobel prize in 2015. Because apart from its success with animals, Ivermectin also worked on people. Over four billion treatments have been donated by pharmaceutical company Merck in an ongoing effort to eliminate river blindness and elephantiasis, in remote tropical regions Link Ivermectin is not registered for human consumption in SA, so it’s quite difficult to come by, on the other hand, the veterinary formulation is usually quite easily available. You just needed to go down to your local co-op Commentary Three But that all changed in early January, because WhatsApp groups across the platteland were abuzz that Ivermectin could also possibly work against Covid-19. Phil Rawlins is a dairy and sheep farmer, and uses Ivermectin on his herds, but suddenly it was difficult to find. Farmer Phil We struggle to get Ivermectin. The shelves are empty, it looks like people are going crazy ko-ops are not just for the farmers anymore. City people are also coming to buy Ivermectin Commentary Four Professor Vinny Naidoo, a veterinary pharmacologist and dean of the faculty of veterinary science, is astonished by this scramble for the veterinary formulation of Ivermectin Professor So we have received reports of Ivermectin being bought in mass volumes from all the farm shops, in fact it’s almost impossible to find Ivermectin anywhere. We have reports of farmers prescribing to family and friends, people selling it at excessively high prices. The drug is actually very cheap- R1.50 per ml, and I heard reports of people selling it for R100 per dose, so its created this black market and that in itself is dangerous. LINK By April last year as deaths began mounting, scientists and doctors started experimenting with drugs that are already available. In Australia they added a single dose of Ivermectin into a petri dish with the virus and cell culture. Within 48 hours the virus was dead Commentary Five But drugs that are miracles in a petri dish, can still disappoint in a human body. Hydroxychloroquine was hyped as a Covid treatment, but later found to be a dud. Professor Helen Rees, chairperson of the South African health products regulatory authority, explains Helen Rees Some things might look very hopeful we saw that with Remdesivir with a smaller study, followed by a larger study that said it didn’t work. We saw that with Hydroxychloroquine, hopeful data initially from smaller studies, larger studies didn’t work. Commentary Six As Covid-19 overwhelmed hospitals in Argentina, Mexico and Egypt, doctors had little to work with, and turned to Ivermectin in desperation. By December of 2020, a group of international physicians, who examined those early trials, told a United States senate hearing, Ivermectin could be the answer to the disease Dr Kory mountains of data have emerged in the last few months. It basically obliterates transmission of this virus. If you take it you will not get sick.” Commentary Seven It was largely this presentation by Dr Kory of the Frontline Covid-19 Critical care alliance that sent South African farmers to storm the ko-ops. Phil Rawlins If I am honest I don’t think it’s dangerous. I have used it myself and I still feel good. Professor There are numerous concerns when it comes to using a veterinary formulation. Firstly it’s illegal to use a veterinary formulation , secondly we don’t know anything about this formulation. Phil Rawlins We took a chance at this stage. I must say I feel good, I am going to carry on taking it and hope I don’t get Covid Masa Prof talk to us a little bit more about the side effects? Professor We know that Ivermectin in animals can cause paralysis just like in the parasite in interferes with the nerve function, it interferes with the brain, and you can have a progressive type of stupor, the animal appears blind and they go into a coma and it’s very difficult to recover them from that. It’s no different to the side-effects you see in people. Commentary eight Alarmed by what was unfolding, the South African Health products regulatory authority, declared Ivermectin illegal and banned its import. That set it on a collision course with a group of SA doctors. Dr Boitumelo Semete-Makokotlela is the CEO Masa Why did SAHPRA ban the importation of Ivermectin? Dr Semete So any drug that is not registered by us as a regulator, is regarded as a drug used unlawfully because you are not complying with the medicines act. We’ve got reports of businessmen just bringing in this product and they are not authorized some of them have no experience in the pharmaceutical sector so it does pose a risk for the public. Commentary nine But the banning led to two unintended consequences. The first was that smugglers jumped on the band wagon. Late in January six Indian nationals were arrested and later charged for illegally importing around R6 million rand’s worth of Ivermectin in their luggage Magistrate Schutte The matter is now postponed to 16th March 2021. Bail is fixed in the amount of R50 000 Masa What we saw happen after that were hundreds of thousands of tablets smuggled into the country. That created an even bigger problem? Dr Boitumelo- Semete No it did. It did. Our law enforcement teams were inundated with inspections of these products. That is one of the reasons we said let’s have a controlled mechanism where we would know who was licensed and anyone else not licensed they will have to deal with the might of the law Up sound Facebook farmer Maybe it tastes very bad. I will squirt it at the back of my mouth Commentary ten The second consequence was that patients began to self -medicate with the veterinary medicine as a prophylaxis. Facebook Farmer On the contrary it doesn’t taste bad at all Commentary eleven And as the second wave intensified, patients began to pressurize their doctors. At the time Johannesburg doctor Paul Freinkel, shared his thoughts in a letter to online newspaper Daily Maverick Paul Freinkel up sound The threat of death hangs in the very air we breathe, it has not felt so close, or so frequent since my internship at the peak of the HIV pandemic ...the punishing hours, the exhaustion, the helplessness the fear of infection... Now we wear masks visors and gowns modern amulets warding off unseen demons Government then didn’t care. Now we uncle Cyril’s ...while we watch our patients suffocate in their own body fluids Masa The million dollar question is, does it work for covid-19? Dr Freinkel One has to look at the data and the data is starting to say that it probably will. And it looks like it is, but we need more data. Commentary Twelve Dr Freinkel read extensively, independently evaluating the 2020 trials cited by the Front line covid critical care alliance, as well as the data from scientist Dr Andrew Hill, and he came to his own conclusions. Masa So would you say it's safe? Dr Freinkel It's not without its complications, every drug has its benefits and side effects. The benefit must always outweigh the risk. And it would appear, given the safety profile of ivermectin, that the potential benefits as far as the data shows us now and it is incomplete, but the potential benefit far outweighs the potential risk if used correctly. Commentary Thirteen What is also dividing doctors and scientists is the dosage for Covid, and only randomized clinical trials can put that to rest. Link Randomized clinical trials are the gold standard to measure a drug’s efficacy. In the case of ivermectin – there have been clinical trials that show positive results. But our scientists aren’t accepting them. Commentary Fourteen Professor Rees says bigger trials are needed Professor Helen Rees So Ivermectin looked promising- the problem is that the studies that were designed to evaluate Ivermectin were small studies, not targeting the same groups of patients, had different indications different dosages, different, formulations and because of that, it’s been extremely difficult to make very firm conclusions Masa Is that the reason why you and other South African scientists aren’t accepting the results coming from all over the world? Professor Helen Rees No it’s not a matter of not accepting the results, what is happening for SAHPRA three different national official bodies have looked at the data. We need large studies that are properly designed to answer this question one way or another. So at the moment we have this situation where we can’t say it works and we can’t say it doesn’t work – and we also need to know if it does work is it safe in the kind of doses that would be required to make it work. We don’t have any of those answers and against that backdrop we need more science. Commentary Fifteen And more science is coming. Stellenbosch university is part of the together Covid-19 trial consortium and they are currently in discussions to test ivermectin and other drugs, during our anticipated third wave. In the meantime SAHPRA have softened its stance and doctors can now use Ivermectin on a case by case basis. Paul When this argument first started, we had different army camps, almost religious in their points of view. We will. We won't. We want to use it. You won't. And now I think I think people are coming to the senses and saying, well, what's the harm? And leaving it to a doctor to decide, which is what doctors are trained to do on the balance of probability is it going to help and is it safe? THE END 11 02. PROMO ONE There are only two real questions in the Ivermectin debate. Does it work for covid-19 and is it safe. And it’s the answers to those questions that have divided the scientific community PROMO TWO The Ivermectin debate rages on, as our scientists call for better clinical trials to find out once and for all if this anti parasitic drug is the miracle some doctors say it is. PROMO THREE Doctors are repurposing drugs, hoping they will work against the Corona virus. There has been hype and disappointment. Now Ivermectin is the latest drug dividing scientists. metadata.Summary: In January, across the platteland a low level frenzy took place. Farmers, doctors, and regular people inundated Ko-ops to get their stash of the veterinary medicine IVOMEC- an anti- parasitic for their sheep and cattle that is the most profitable veterinary medicine of all time. Why? Because they have been convinced that this medicine will keep them Covid or at least death free, and even if our scientists who are some of the best in the world have expressed their reservations, men in two tone shirts are injecting themselves, their families and their workers with Ivermectin. When in early January SAHPRA banned the import of Ivermectin, it didn’t take long for the criminals and opportunists to jump on the band wagon and bring in about 150 thousand contraband tablets in their luggage. For their efforts they were arrested and are out on R50 000 bail. So does it work and is it safe? That is the million dollar question and one that Carte Blanche will try and answer by speaking to a doctor on the frontline a world renowned scientist and As 2021 dawned we all hoped that the worst of the pandemic was over. But that spiky little virus is not done with us yet. 30 000 deaths, a rapidly increasing second wave and a tricksy variant has our health department on the back foot once again. We are out of options and out of money, and our vaccine rollout could still take months before it really makes an impact on most of us. So, South Africans are doing what they always do – they are making a plan, and refusing to wait for the high priests of medicine to give them the go ahead -they are taking Ivermectin in a desperate and reckless attempt to keep the virus at bay.
metadata.Further information: THE FRONT LINE COVID CRITICAL CARE ALLIANCE AND DR KORY The frenzy began when an American physician, Dr Kory appeared at a Senate hearing in December. He told the committee that he belonged to a group of highly published physicians in the world and they had been reviewing the literature of all drugs to try and find a solution to Covid 19. “We have done nothing but try to figure out how to identify a repurpose available drugs to treat this illness.” He expressed his concern that the solutions being touted were about novel and expensive pharmaceutical drugs. He said he was “severely troubled by the fact that the FDA, the NAH and the CDC have done nothing to review repurposed drugs to treat this disease.” He said: “We have 100 years of medicine development and we do not know of a task force that has been constituted to evaluate available drugs.” He says Ivermectin has a miraculous impact but he doesn’t want to be sensational when he says that. “It’s a scientific evaluation based on mountains of data that has emerged in the last few months. It basically obliterates transmission of this virus. If you take it he says you will not get sick.” He quotes a trial from Argentina where he says 800 health care workers used it as a prophylactic and not one not get sick. He says it has immense and potent anti- viral activity. He quotes different trials and says four randomized trials in hospitals show reduced mortality. “It is proving to be a wonder drug” says Dr Kory.” Its already won the Nobel prize for medicine in 2015 for the eradication of parasitic diseases. With this kind of sales pitch it’s hard to blame the farmers for trusting an American physician in a white coat, telling a senate hearing that the drug works. Who can blame them for putting their trust in a first world doctor, when our own president told them less than two weeks ago that the vaccine was still months away, and the health ministers webinar gave few specifics and was criticized by Dr Mahdi as aspirational rather than a specific plan? But we have been down this road before – most notably with Hydroxychloroquine- touted as a miracle by no less than the President of the USA. And we know where that went. Not only was the drug dangerous it also didn’t work. As conspiracy theorists jumped back on their bandwagon, the Department of health did ask our scientists and top pharmacists for a quick review . On the 21st December they summarized their finding • • The overall quality of the randomized trials involving ivermectin in COVID‐19 patients is extremely low. • From the available randomised control trial evidence, ivermectin is not superior to placebo in terms of viral load reduction or clinical progression. There is no evidence from randomised control trials for any reduction in mortality. Eligible patients with COVID‐19 in South Africa should be considered for enrolment in relevant therapeutic trials. This is what they had to say in an open letter: The Ivermectin Interest Group ("IIG") is a grouping of clinicians, public health specialists, community health workers and scientists that have an interest in exploring the potential of the medicine Ivermectin to both prevent and treat COVID-19. While we fully endorse the pursuit and implementation of all available evidence-based vaccines, as they are essential to ending the pandemic, we wish to ensure that the potential of promising preventive and therapeutic measures, including drugs, be fully and urgently investigated. IVERMECTIN Currently, the use of Ivermectin is controversial for sound scientific reasons. We acknowledge that the drug has not been indicated for use in COVID-19 prophylaxis or treatment, either locally or by the major regulatory bodies globally. However, we must note that Ivermectin has been the subject of a number of studies and reviews, including a review funded by the World Health Organisation (WHO) as part of the ACT Accelerator and UNITAID programmes (Hill et al., 2020) that concluded that urgent further trials are required and that results anticipated from clinical trials currently underway will be available in January 2021 and could provide the numbers required for a meta-analysis to provide a reliable outcome.
